request.prompt: Tender, sorrowful cinematic orchestral music at 76 BPM in a minor key, intimate and restrained, written for a battle where the heroine must fight someone she loves. A solo grand piano carries a simple, aching, singing melody over gentle broken-chord accompaniment; a warm string orchestra enters softly, then a solo cello and a solo violin trade a mournful line. A soft heartbeat pulse of low strings and a muted timpani underneath, with no cymbals and no heroic brass. It swells slowly to a heartfelt, tearful peak with the full strings and a few sustained French horns, then recedes to the solo piano so it can repeat. Bittersweet, gentle, sad but dignified, never triumphant. Entirely real acoustic instruments recorded in a warm concert hall. Steady tempo, no tempo changes, no fade-out, no final cadence. Not chiptune, not SNES, not arcade, no synthesizers, no electronic drums, no electric guitar, no pop, no vocals.
